# Ulcer Index (`ulcer_index`)

*Category: Drawdowns · Nature: observed · Unit: decimal_return · Formula id: `ulcer_index@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Root-mean-square drawdown: combines depth and duration of declines.

## 2. Formula

```text
sqrt( (1/n) * sum_t D_t^2 )
```

## 3. Required inputs

Periodic simple returns.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Lower is better.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

A single number for how deep and how long-lasting the declines were; 0 means the investment never fell below a previous high.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Martin & McCann's Ulcer Index on the canonical drawdown path; the denominator of the Martin ratio (Ulcer Performance Index).

## 7. Assumptions

- Drawdowns measured from running peaks of compounded wealth.

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- Short histories: drawdown statistics grow with the length of the track record and cannot reveal risks that have not yet materialized.
- Compared across data frequencies.

## 9. Minimum sensible data

One observation; low confidence below 3 years. (policy `path_risk`: Path statistics (drawdowns, streaks) are computable from one observation but are unrepresentative below 3 years (low) and 5 years (moderate); longer histories tend to reveal deeper drawdowns.)

## 10. Reference implementations

| Library | Function | Agrees | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| PerformanceAnalytics 2.0.4 (R) | `UlcerIndex` | no (documented difference) | PerformanceAnalytics 2.0.4 builds drawdowns with DrawdownPeak, which divides returns by 100 (assumes percent inputs); agreement is verified against sqrt(mean(Drawdowns(R)^2)) instead. |

## 11. Sources

- Martin, P. G., & McCann, B. B. (1989). The Investor's Guide to Fidelity Funds. Wiley (Ulcer Index and Ulcer Performance Index).
- Bacon, C. R. (2021). Practical Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement (2nd ed.). Wiley.

## 12. OpenFactsheet convention

Non-negative magnitude in decimal units, computed from the canonical drawdown path over observations 1..n.
